newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsicans attack police barracks, make new threats.
newsitem.headline: Corsicans attack police barracks, make new threats.

text.p: Gunmen shot at a police barracks on the Mediterranean island of Corsica on Thursday as island separatists made fresh threats against a golf course bombed last week in an alleged extortion attempt, police said.
In the shooting incident, paramilitary gendarmes said eight bullets hit their barracks in Saint-Florent but no police were injured.
A sentry returned fire as the attackers fled, pursued by police cars.
Though they managed to escape, police sources said they found bloodstains in the attackers' abandoned car.
The attack bore the hallmarks of the outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC)-Historic Wing, which on Thursday claimed responsibility for seven previous attacks this week.
"Our commandos will no longer take useless risks," the FLNC said in an open letter. "The gendarmes should see their situation as a state of war".

The wave of attacks on government buildings followed Monday's arrest of the island's best-known separatist leader Francois Santoni who was taken into custody in connection with the bombing attack on the Sperone golf course and an earlier weapons violation.

Santoni, head of Cuncolta Naziunalista, the legal party of the outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC), and his lawyer girlfriend Marie-Helene Mattei were remanded and placed under investigation for attempted extortion and bomb attacks.
Nonetheless, the FLNC boldly issued a second statement on Thursday warning the golf course owner against using or repairing the facility.
According to its owner, a house belonging to the course's caretaker was blown up after the owner refused separatists' demand for four million francs ($800,000) in protection money.

Another suspected separatist guerrilla, Piere Convaix, was taken to Paris on Thursday for questioning. He was arrested on the island driving a car packed with explosives and gas containers with two other suspects.
The government ordered a crackdown after separatists stepped up attacks in a two-decade-old campaign to demand greater autonomy from Paris for the Mediterranean holiday island.
